issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court’s power under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to transfer a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act remains available notwithstanding the non obstante clause in Section 142(1) of that Act.

A complaint under Section 138 cannot be transferred under Section 406 on the ground of lack of territorial jurisdiction before the relevant jurisdictional facts are established by evidence; the trial court must decide that objection under the applicable criminal procedure rules.

Under Section 142(2)(a) and its Explanation, territorial jurisdiction over a cheque-dishonour complaint is determined by the bank account through which the cheque is delivered for collection, including the statutory deeming rule for delivery at another branch.

Transfer under Section 406 requires circumstances making transfer necessary in the interests of justice, and inconvenience or language difficulties alone do not justify transferring a case from a court that has territorial jurisdiction.
